title: Model Context Protocol: the problem it solves

videos.script: Lessons eight, nine and ten wrote the same order lookup three times, once for each library, and each library described it to its model in a different format. That is the problem the Model Context Protocol exists to solve. {{title}} In this lesson the lookup is written once, as an MCP server, and the three hosts use it unchanged. {{once}} Their clients did not even speak the same revision of the protocol. One used the revision of July twenty twenty-six, with no handshake; two used the one before it, with a handshake. The server answered both. {{revisions}} Then what MCP standardises and what it leaves to the host: the model, the loop, and every decision about permission. {{scope}} And when a server is worth its cost, and when a function in your own program is the better tool. {{last}}
